thread:
pagerbot: PAGER: critical - multiple multi-GPU training allocations are failing with NCCL communicator errors and CUDA watchdog resets on node gpu-78. Incident INC-2170001234. Please acknowledge.

leila: acked. Picking up pager. Which tenants affected and any customer-visible endpoints?

pagerbot: Affected queue: training-batch. 12 jobs failed across 3 tenants (delta-vision, epoch-labs, sigma-ml). Some long-running tuning jobs retried; no public API endpoints impacted right now. Error signal: NCCL comm aborts + CUDA kernel watchdog resets + occasional container OOM events.

omar: paste the container stdout and dmesg. We need the exact NCCL/CUDA lines to decide fallback.

leila: logs from one failed job:
```
2026-03-16T01:04:18Z ERROR trainer: nccl: Unhandled system error. ncclCommInitAll failed.
NCCL ERROR WATCHDOG  : aborted at 0x7f9c00
CUDA Error: device-side assert triggered (701) gpu=1
RuntimeError: CUDA error: device-side assert triggered
```

frank: host dmesg shows repeated GPU reset messages and PCIe AER counts incrementing around 01:03:
```
[  78.901234] nvidia 0000:0a:00.0: GPU fault detected: 0x10f2
[  78.901567] pcieport 0000:05:00.0: AER: Multiple corrected error received
[  79.002345] ksoftirqd: dropped IRQ rate spike
```

omar: interestingly, kernel's oom_reaper also ran on container cgroups: `oom-killer invoked for pid 2345` in some instances. Could be cascading resource pressure after resets.

leila: immediate actions: 1) cordon and drain node gpu-78; 2) apply emergency routing to single-GPU variants for affected tenants; 3) capture full nv-host dump and cgroup snapshots; 4) avoid killing jobs until checkpoints snapshotted. I'll execute.

ops-bot: Cordoning gpu-78. No new pods will schedule. Evicting existing pods gracefully (grace period 120s).

deploy-bot: Routing patch recommended. Example patch:
```yaml
routes:
  - tenant: epoch-labs
    override:
      use_single_gpu: true
    duration: 45m
    reason: emergency-fallback
```
Apply via `rictl apply -f route-emergency.yaml`.

leila: applied fallbacks for delta-vision and epoch-labs. sigma-ml declined auto-fallback (manual job critical) - they're being notified.

frank: I've started full nv-host diagnostic: `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=utilization.gpu,enc,dec,temperature.gpu,mem_error --format=csv -q` and saved dumps to s3://rt-incidents/2170001234/host-dumps/.

omar: for multi-GPU communicators, a transient fabric partition will cause rank mismatch and NCCL watchdog aborts. Quick mitigations to keep customers moving: set environment overrides for routing and for new jobs: `NCCL_IB_DISABLE=1` (force TCP/ethernet), `NCCL_P2P_LEVEL=PXB`, and lower `NCCL_TOPO_DONT_REORDER=1` while we investigate. Use these only for canaries.

leila: enacting `NCCL_IB_DISABLE=1` on the scheduler side for new allocations in the affected AZ. Pushing env through job-profile overlay.

ops-bot: Env overlay applied to new jobs in az-west-3. Existing jobs left intact.

frank: node drain progress: 10/12 pods evicted. Two jobs appear stuck in the runtime's watchdog loop and not responding to `kubectl exec`. I'll snapshot their volumes (logs+checkpoints) before force-delete.

leila: do snapshot and then force-delete. Use `kubectl delete pod --grace-period=30 --force` after snapshot complete.

ops-bot: Snapshots uploaded to s3://rt-incidents/2170001234/snapshots/. Size: 2.4GB.

omar: scheduling immediate driver reload and node reboot. Before reboot, pull PCIe AER counters and NVLINK error counts: `cat /sys/class/infiniband/*/errors` and `nvidia-smi -q -d ECC,PERF,LINK` to attach to vendor ticket.

frank: rebooting node now. Logging vendor ticket VT-11021 with attached logs and nv-host dumps.

pagerbot: Severity set to Sev2 due to tenant retries and >10 jobs impacted. Pager escalation path notified.

eve-cs: customer update sent to delta-vision and epoch-labs: "We're investigating an internal multi-GPU fabric issue causing job retries. We've routed jobs to single-GPU fallbacks where possible and are performing hardware maintenance. We'll update in 45m."

leila: after reboot, node shows all GPUs present but NVLINK error counters non-zero:
```
$ nvidia-smi -q -d NVLINK
NVLINK Link 0: Correctable ECC errors: 6
NVLINK Link 1: Correctable ECC errors: 0
```

omar: six correctable NVLINK errors is concerning; vendor recommends replacement if count stays >5 after reboot and stress test. Starting a 20m nvlink stress.

frank: started canary multi-GPU job with reduced batch-size and NCCL_DEBUG=INFO, under observation. Also disabled IB for new jobs. Canary ran for 15m without watchdog reset.

leila: policy decision: keep node out of regular rotation for 8 hours and schedule hardware swap if NVLINK counters increase during stress. I've labeled node `hardware:under-investigation`.

omar: additional mitigation: scheduler admission control change proposal - when a node reports any NVLINK AER events, prevent multi-GPU scheduling on that node automatically. Will follow up as a repo PR.

frank: vendor ticket VT-11021 updated with the latest counters and nvlink stress results. If vendor approves replacement, they'll send RMA.

eve-cs: confirmed with customers that no persistent data loss observed; some training runs retried from last checkpoint. Customers request a short RCA by tomorrow morning.

leila: handoff to night ops: @omar will monitor; summary + artifacts in incident doc: https://console.redwood.ai/incidents/2170001234. Key runbook steps included in doc.

omar: acknowledged. I'll watch nvlink counters and the vendor ticket. If correctable errors increase beyond threshold or if NCCL watchdogs reappear, escalate to immediate hardware swap.

pagerbot: Incident INC-2170001234 status: mitigated -> monitoring. Auto-close candidate in 12h unless regression.

leila: postmortem actions captured:
- root cause hypothesis: transient NVLINK/PCIe fabric errors -> GPU watchdog resets -> NCCL communicator aborts -> cascaded job retries
- mitigations performed: drain node, env overrides (NCCL_IB_DISABLE), single-GPU fallbacks, driver reload and reboot, nvlink stress test, vendor ticket opened
- follow-ups: implement scheduler rule to avoid multi-GPU placement on nodes with AER events, add NVLINK-correctable threshold alert, document single-GPU emergency routing in runbook, and prepare customer RCA template.

frank: creating post-incident doc and attaching artifacts. Ticket VT-11021 linked.

eve-cs: I'll send the RCA draft to customers in the morning with a timeline and mitigation summary.

omar: switching channel to read-only. Night team will reopen if anomalies detected.

leila: thanks all. Closing active coordination.
